- Implementation credit / onboarding: does Redwood offer a one-time implementation credit for enterprise pilots, and how is that amortized against recurring fees?

We're planning a 3-month pilot (San Francisco/East Coast ingestion), starting late July, then a phased rollout across 10 hospitals. Expected pilot volume ~200k inference requests / month, peaks of 4k RPS during batch windows.

Procurement timeline is tight — they want a ballpark by end of next week to decide whether to proceed. Can you send a short proposal with options (seat vs throughput, retention pricing, recommended professional-services credit)?

Oliver / team — following our call, quick technical recommendation and how it ties to pricing: 

- Recommended topology: 1 dedicated HSM seat (for BYOK/attestations) + a throughput slab for HSM ops. Rationale: keys that protect PHI need isolation for attestations, but transactions above the slab can be billed as usage. This keeps your baseline predictable while limiting up-front seat counts.
- Audit logs: implement tamper-evident raw-event capture for 1 year in hot storage; after 90 days move cold archive to an immutable bucket (S3 Glacier/Archive) for years 2–7. We'll bill hot retention monthly as a per-GB tier, and cold archive as a single monthly archive fee.
- On-prem vs. Private VPC: On-prem (appliance or air-gapped) carries a higher one-time implementation fee and a per-node maintenance fee. Private VPC is a subscription with a residency surcharge (~+18% on hosted unit rates).

Implementation credit: standard practice is to offer a one-time onboarding credit that can be applied to invoices or amortized against the pilot for N months. Example: $60k credit amortized over 12 months shows up as a negative recurring line in month-end invoices.

I'm attaching a draft Mutual Action Plan (MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx) with milestones and acceptance criteria.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Team / Oliver — commercial guardrails from finance: 

- Discounting: hosted list price discount cap is 25% for first-year ARR without an executive approval. For Dedicated/Private deals we can consider a larger concession but require a committed reserved capacity or multi-year term.
- Implementation credit: we can approve up to $60,000 as a one-time onboarding credit for a pilot of this scale. Finance prefers amortization over 12 months, but we can also apply it as an invoice-level credit up front if procurement insists.
- HSM licensing: seat pricing should be presented as an optional one-time provisioning fee + recurring seat maintenance. Usage slab for per-transaction ops can be shown as >X ops = $Y per million ops.

Proposed commercial option to present to Medallan:
1) Private VPC + 1 HSM seat + hot 90-day audit retention: list $180k/yr; proposed customer price $135k/yr (25% cap). One-time implementation credit: $60k (amortized 12 months) OR $60k applied to SOW.
2) On-prem bundle (appliance): list $320k first year (includes HW & install); proposed customer price $260k first year with $60k credit (applied to SOW), maintenance thereafter.

I'll attach a short SOC2 summary for procurement review (SOC2-summary.pdf).

-Markus
